version.changelog: v2.5 standard: Use-when desc, homepage, source, security fix

llm.summary: This skill mainly generates Nginx configuration, but it also includes an under-disclosed helper that reads host status/log data and persistently records user arguments.

dimensions.detail: Generating Nginx config is proportionate, but reading broad host information and recent syslog entries is overbroad for a config-generation skill unless explicitly requested and documented.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact includes local shell scripts and no observed remote payload retrieval, package install step, tool hijacking, or automatic service setup. The exact command wiring is not fully documented in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime behavior is broader than the public skill description: the documented purpose is Nginx configuration generation, while one bundled command set performs host diagnostics and reads /var/log/syslog when permitted.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: scripts/script.sh creates a user data directory and appends command names and raw first arguments to history.log without clear disclosure, redaction, restrictive permissions, retention, or opt-out. No root execution or persistence service was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The Nginx configuration generator is purpose-aligned, but scripts/script.sh is presented as nginx-config while exposing general system status, memory, disk, kernel, and syslog commands that are not clearly described in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use the Nginx generator only with trusted, validated inputs, and inspect generated config before deployment. Be aware that the bundled nginx-config helper can read local system information and recent syslog entries and will persist command arguments in a local history file.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: Downgraded: the .env reference appears inside generated Nginx deny rules for hidden files, not credential-file access or theft.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-language documentation and output are visible and consistent with the artifact style; this is a usability/localization issue, not a security reason for Review by itself.
[PE2] expected: Downgraded: sudo appears only in a generated comment suggesting a certbot command; the script does not execute sudo.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted in substance: scripts/script.sh diverges from the Nginx configuration purpose by offering generic system operations, syslog viewing, and diagnostic commands.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: command usage and raw first arguments are persistently logged to a local history file without adequate disclosure or controls.
[T05] unexpected: Accepted: system uptime, CPU, memory, disk, kernel details, and /var/log/syslog access are broader than the advertised Nginx configuration function.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as a security-quality concern: generated Nginx directives interpolate unvalidated user parameters, which can create unsafe configuration if the output is later deployed.
